messages:
angela: Quick FYI — I'm about to propose a minimal RBAC change for the on‑prem keystore agent in the priv-deploy staging cluster. Goal: remove broad `keystore-admin` clusterrole binding and replace with a least-privilege role scoped to the `keystore` namespace.

peter: +1 on least-priv. Can you state the exact permissions you need? I want to validate there’s no accidental access to control-plane secrets.

angela: Current plan: new Role `keystore-agent-reader` in `keystore` ns with `get,list,watch` on `secrets` and `pods` and a separate `keystore-agent-rotate` role with `update` only on `secrets/keystore-certs`. No clusterrole.

carlos: Does that break our audit pipeline? We have retention rules that expect agent writes to be stamped with service-account <keystore-agent@redwood>. Need assurance audit logs still capture both KMS requests and secret writes.

jen: Also flag: when you tighten RBAC, the agent loses ability to upload rotation events to the central audit collector unless we explicitly allow `pods/exec` or a write to the collector svc. Prefer not to open exec. Suggest explicit `create` on `events` in `keystore`.

angela: Good catch. I'll add `create` on `events` and `create` on a namespaced `auditlogs` CRD if present. For KMS calls (external HSM), the service account still uses the same IAM creds via the node identity — that won’t change.

peter: On KMS integration: are we relying on local keystore to call KMS directly, or proxying through control plane? We should avoid control-plane egress from isolated VPCs.

angela: Local agent calls KMS endpoint in customer VPC (HSM or cloud KMS). There’s a small outbound allowlist for KMS IPs; network team verified it’s narrow. We must document the allowlist in the runbook.

sec-bot: [automated] Reminder: run RBAC dry-run validation: `rbac-checker --config=priv-keystore-rbacs.yaml --dry-run`

carlos: About audit logging: if any of the secret writes fail (403), we need an observable alert. Can we add a Prom rule to fire on `keystore_agent_errors_total{code="403"}`?

jen: Yes, add the rule and a thumbnail runbook link. Also add a grafana panel for KMS latency percentiles — if KMS is slow, rotation can stall and escalate to incident.

angela: Will do. Also planning a small netpol change: deny all ingress into `keystore` ns except from `metrics` and `controlplane-proxy`. Using explicit allow rules instead of default deny to reduce risk. Draft NP below:

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-from-proxy-and-metrics
  namespace: keystore
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          k8s-app: controlplane-proxy
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: metrics-collector
```

peter: That looks tight. Ensure we also allow the node kubelet CNI healthchecks if needed. Some CNIs use hostNetwork probes.

angela: Good point — will add a hostNetwork exception annotation on the policy and test.

carlos: Vulnerability triage note: the external scanner flagged an old dependency in the keystore agent container (openssl). We have a patch rolling; test that the new image has identical behavior before we apply RBAC changes. Can't combine both changes in one rollout.

jen: Agreed — separate rollouts. RBAC + NP first (safest), then image patch. If RBAC rollout causes failures, we can immediately revert binding; keep canary at 5% for 2 hours.

angela: Plan for incident response if RBAC misconfig => agents fail to read secrets: 1) Alert by prom rule, 2) run `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:keystore:agent get secrets/keystore-certs`, 3) if denied, reapply previous binding and open incident channel #priv-deploy-ops, 4) gather audit logs and KMS request traces.

sec-bot: [automated] Runbook link created: https://confluence.internal/redwood/priv-keystore-rbac-runbook — includes rollback commands and checklist.

peter: One more: add short-lived elevated creds procedure for SRE to troubleshoot inside customer VPC (time-limited token, recorded session). We can’t rely on static breakglass keys.

carlos: +1 on ephemeral jumpbox sessions and mandatory session recording. Compliance will want the session logs.

angela: Thanks — I'll prepare the PR with the Role/RoleBinding diffs, NP draft, Prom rule, and a checklist for the runbook. Will tag @peter @carlos @jen for review. :thumbsup:

jen: Thanks — please include test matrix: smoke read, rotate, audit event present, and netpol connectivity tests.

angela: Will do. Targeting staging rollout tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

peter: ACK.
